scope: Read-only verification of Batch 76 script, backup, log, and incident-provenance claims.

improvements: All four embedded script bodies are internally consistent with their declared byte lengths and SHA-256 hashes.
Creation script contents and filesystem timestamps materially support the coder-fixture explanation.
Coder explicitly declares that no database pre-deletion image or binlog exists instead of fabricating one.
limitations: Hashes prove only the embedded bytes; the artifact does not include an independently timestamped capture binding those bytes to the server paths before deletion.
The 01:16 UTC backup predates orders 335, 362, 469, and 470, so its zero-order state cannot classify orders 469 or 470.
Absence of transactional email is corroboration, not proof of non-customer origin; the second creation script disables email and the first allegedly timed out in email handling.
The scripts set neither created_via nor a persisted fixture marker, and no raw pre-deletion rows or execution transcript are attached.
No independently attributable owner/operator incident disposition is attached.

decision.reason: Batch 76 materially raises confidence that 469 and 470 were coder fixtures, but cannot prove row-level provenance after permanent deletion. R107 explicitly required owner/operator review when pre-deletion evidence is unavailable; that governance gate remains missing.

requiredNextAction: Stop generating additional self-authored forensic summaries.
Check whether the hosting provider has a snapshot between 22:45 and 22:56 UTC; if available, obtain a read-only redacted extract for orders 469 and 470.

If no such snapshot exists, obtain an independently attributable owner/operator incident disposition acknowledging the evidence boundary, deciding whether 469 and 470 may be treated as fixtures, and accepting or rejecting closure.
Keep the mutation moratorium and do not touch orders 335 or 362.
